name: Mixosaurus
provenance: Middle Triassic · Besano Formation, Monte San Giorgio
description: Small early ichthyosaur with the oldest dorsal fin of any backboned animal, long forefins, short hindfins and a lobed tail. Authored Tripo body and measured procedural volume twin share one armature, one set of inverse binds, one set of sockets and one set of actions.
notes: Carangiform, not anguilliform: half a wavelength on the body, the front third almost still, and the amplitude piled into the peduncle. The research calls this animal more fish-like than its basal relatives, and it is built to read against Cymbospondylus.

The dorsal fin -- the oldest in any backboned animal, and this animal's headline -- is the generation's own blade on its own seated joint. It is a keel: it holds the line at sprint and leans into a turn and a dart, and it never flaps.
Dart is a C-start, the roster's shoalDart: the whole body folds one way in a sixth of a second and snaps through straight. It is not a short Attack.

The body was measured into its own frame before anything was rigged: this generation lies 25.2 degrees across the file axes -- the most crooked of the four -- and its roll was read off the countershading rather than transported.

This generation has **no modelled mouth**: Placodus' geometric method finds nothing on the rostrum, so the mouth line was read off the albedo as Dinocephalosaurus' was. There is therefore no source dentition either, and none was authored; see the README.

The caudal fin is deeply forked with two near-equal lobes, which the research denies this animal -- "not the post-Triassic lunate fluke". That is the pose and the generation, recorded rather than remodelled; see the README.
The twin resurfaces a voxel occupancy field of the authored body, relaxes it and reduces the new topology. It reuses no source vertex or face.
Living colours, soft tissues and movements are artistic reconstruction. World travel remains engine-owned.
